name: coverage-gap-analysis
title: Coverage Gap Analysis — HRA Modeling White-Space (Planned)
question:
Which HRA organs and FTUs have ZERO mechanistic-model coverage even at
full-corpus scale (635/1,730 AS nodes covered across 31/114 organ GLBs),
and can they be ranked into a prioritized modeling-gap report?

study_card.goal: Cross the full corpus-coverage organ->models index against the complete 114-organ-GLB / 1,730-AS-node crosswalk to list every organ/AS-node with zero covering models, ranked by AS-node count, as a prioritized modeling-gap report.
study_card.mechanism: Planned: a gap-report Step reusing corpus-coverage's coverage/coverage_summary output, inverting the covered-set against the full crosswalk to enumerate the complement (uncovered organs/AS-nodes) and rank it by AS-node count per organ.
study_card.expected_result: A ranked list of the 83 organs (114 minus the 31 already covered) with zero mechanistic-model coverage, surfacing which carry the most AS nodes (i.e. the highest-value modeling targets) at the top.
study_card.main_expert_question: Does the low 7.5% organ-tagging yield undercount real anatomical relevance among the untagged 1,014 models — i.e. is the 'white-space' this study reports really unmodeled biology, or partly an artifact of the current name-only tagger's recall ceiling (see sbml-annotation-tagging)?
study_card.future_work: The real gap-ranking composite is not yet implemented. This scaffold's baseline placeholder reuses the existing corpus-coverage composite purely so the study resolves and renders; the enumeration/ranking mechanism itself is future work.

biological_summary:
corpus-coverage established that crossing the full 1,096-model curated
BioModels catalog against the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk covers 635/1,730 AS
nodes (36.7%) across 31/114 organ GLBs (27.2%) — an order of magnitude
wider than a single search query, and wide enough to newly reach kidney.
That leaves 83 organs and their associated AS nodes with no mechanistic
model at all in the current index: the "dark" (unmodeled) anatomy this
study aims to enumerate and rank, so downstream modeling effort (new
curation, new model authorship, or import work like
multiorgan-glucose-m4) can be prioritized toward the organs/FTUs where
covering even one model would unlock the most AS-node coverage.
limitations: TBD — planned study, not yet implemented.

remaining_uncertainties: Which HRA organs/FTUs have zero mechanistic-model coverage even at full-corpus scale (the modeling white-space)?
